sections.h2: Ways to sell in Bonita Springs
sections.html:
When time matters in Bonita Springs, a cash buyer is the usual answer. A listing has to wait on open houses, inspections and whoever is financing the purchase. Many owners in town are dealing with storm repairs, a seasonal second home or an estate, and each of those pushes you toward a different route.

  • Cash buyer: accepts flaws as they stand, and you negotiate the closing day.
  • Agent: broader exposure, with repair and lender dates built into the schedule.
  • Solo sale: you run the contract and the recording yourself.

Lee County's property appraiser, tax collector and clerk each hold part of your file, so begin with the property record for your address. Bonita Springs became a city by vote in 1999, and homes range from older streets to golf course communities. Say plainly how old your house is and what has been updated, and keep permits and repair records ready for the buyer.

sections.h2: Selling a house damaged by Hurricane Ian
sections.html:
If your house was damaged, report it to the Lee County Property Appraiser. The new value is set as of the January 1 after the event, and the damage is factored in. Owners can email hurricaneupdate@leepa.org or use the reporting link on the appraiser's hurricane page.

Residential owners can apply for a partial tax refund depending on the extent of damage and whether the property could be used, with details in section 197.319 of the Florida Statutes. A rebuild that changes the property significantly will likely raise its value, while one similar to the old house should have a minimal effect. Permits are still required under each jurisdiction's process, and the FEMA 50 percent rule applies to substantial repairs. Before spending on a house you mean to sell, ask the city building office which rules reach your job.

For many parcels the appraiser issues a tax roll value letter that helps owners apply the FEMA 50 percent rule, which compares repair cost with the value of the structure. Vacant land, many commercial properties and condominiums may get no letter. There are deadlines for starting repairs if you want to keep a homestead on a damaged house, so email exemptions@leepa.org before deciding between repairing and selling.

  • Condominiums get no tax roll value letter, because the appraiser does not split land and building value for a whole complex.
  • Condo owners can work with their association on a private appraisal of the entire complex.
  • While repairing, do not register to vote or get a driver license elsewhere, or the homestead exemption could be jeopardized. Changing your mailing address is fine.

sections.h2: Lee County property taxes and a sale
sections.html:
Lee County values each parcel on January 1 and sends bills in November. After a sale, the next owner's assessment goes back to market the following January. Homestead relief reaches $50,000 and needs an application filed by March 1. Under Save Our Homes, assessed value may rise each year by the smaller of inflation or 3 percent. The state's chart shows 2.7 percent for 2026.

Lee County tax calendar for sellers
StepWhen it happens
Value dateJanuary 1 each year
Exemption filingMarch 1 with the property appraiser
Notice of proposed taxesMailed in August
BillsSent in November
DelinquentApril 1

Seasonal owners should know that renting the home, or ceasing to live there permanently, ends the homestead. To contest your value, file with the clerk inside 25 days of that August notice.

Florida's deed tax on a Lee County conveyance is 70 cents for each $100 of price. Each signer can be held to it by the state, and the clerk collects it when the deed is recorded.

Statute sets the clerk's recording fees by the page. The deed itself must carry two subscribing witnesses. A deed from a court-appointed representative is left off the state's taxable list, and a spouse's homestead deed is exempt where a mortgage is the only consideration.

Every one of these cases is governed by a state timetable. An estate of up to $150,000, or one opened over two years after the death, may qualify for the shorter summary process, which can speed an heir's sale.

A landlord with a tenant behind on rent may serve written notice giving three days, not counting weekends or court holidays. Foreclosure sales are set 20 to 35 days after judgment.

Unpaid taxes lead to certificate sales by June 1, and a holder may seek a tax deed two years on. Get a payoff figure from the Lee County Tax Collector before you set a closing day.

sections.h2: Steps to close a Bonita Springs sale
sections.html:
1. Search the parcel on the Lee County appraiser's site and note exemptions and any damage report.
  2. Ask your lender for a payoff and the tax collector for your balance.
  3. Check city permit records for open or unpermitted work.
  4. Weigh each route by the money left after taxes and recording fees.
  5. Sign the deed in front of two witnesses, then have the Lee County clerk record it.

A title agent usually handles the search and the settlement statement. Review that statement before signing day and ask about every line you do not recognize. If an offer depends on repairs, get the scope and the deadline in writing so a missed date does not turn into a dispute at the table.

Sellers who show up with documents in hand get quicker answers from buyers and title agents. Pull together your deed, the latest tax bill, any insurance claim file from storm damage, receipts for repairs and photos of finished work. If a contractor did the job, keep the invoice and any final inspection record. Seasonal owners who live elsewhere should also line up a way to sign remotely or name someone with written authority, because a closing date that depends on a plane ticket is easy to miss.

Plan your final week around three jobs. First, schedule utility shutoffs for the day after the deed is recorded, so the buyer is never left without service during the walkthrough. Second, hand over keys, garage openers, gate codes and any warranty paperwork for appliances or the roof. Third, confirm where your proceeds will be sent and who will wire them. Take dated photos of the empty house after you move out, which protects you if a buyer later questions its condition.

Because a cash buyer needs no lender appraisal or loan approval, the weeks normally spent on underwriting fall away. Title work, payoff letters and tax balances still apply, and so does the deed signing. Get proof of funds, a closing date in writing and a clear split of fees from any buyer. Set the offer next to a listing estimate that already subtracts repairs, holding costs and commission, then choose the one that suits your deadline.

faqs.q: Is Bonita Springs in Lee County?
faqs.a: Yes, and the Lee County Property Appraiser values its parcels. Voters made it a city in 1999.

faqs.q: Do I need to tell the appraiser about hurricane damage?
faqs.a: Yes. Value follows the home's condition on the January 1 after the event. Residential owners may also apply for a partial refund under section 197.319.

faqs.q: Can I keep my homestead while repairing a storm-damaged house?
faqs.a: Yes, if you tell the appraiser you intend to repair or rebuild and make it your permanent residence. Avoid actions like registering to vote or getting a license in another county or state.

faqs.q: What is the doc stamp rate in Lee County?
faqs.a: It is 70 cents for each $100 of price. The state can look to any party on the deed, whoever the contract assigns it to.

faqs.q: Does my homestead exemption stay with the house?
faqs.a: No, it leaves with you. The buyer applies by March 1 for a new one, and the parcel is reassessed at market the January after the sale.
